title: Design System: Outside In Bass Lab

display.purpose: Playfair, struck. The title at the head of a page and the wordmark. Never below --t-h3: a didone's hairlines disappear.

headline.purpose: Source Serif. A section within a page.

title.purpose: Source Serif. A subsection or a card heading.

body.purpose: Source Serif, tracking zero. Everything read, at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Inter, 11px uppercase tracked .14em. The engraved plate above a control. Never sets a sentence.

hand.purpose: Caveat in pencil blue, rotated -1.5deg. Asides only, never load-bearing.

readout.purpose: Playfair, tabular lining figures. A number read from across the room: tempo, bar, cents.

notation.purpose: Bravura SMuFL. Real clefs, noteheads and time signatures on real staves.

shadows.name: book
shadows.purpose: The two pages and the instrument strip, cast onto the stand. Used three times in the whole design.

shadows.name: raise
shadows.purpose: A lit top edge and a short shadow, for something resting on the page.

shadows.name: tape
shadows.purpose: The strip of vermillion tape at rest.

shadows.name: tape-lift
shadows.purpose: The tape on hover: the only thing in the design that rises.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: A well cut into the page. Means recessed, never emphasised.

shadows.name: press
shadows.purpose: The active state of a ruled control. The press goes into the page.

shadows.name: knob
shadows.purpose: The travelling knob of a switch.

motion.name: ease-page
motion.purpose: Paper motion: a decelerating curve that settles. The default for everything.

motion.name: ease-mech
motion.purpose: Mechanical travel: a switch knob, a transport key.

motion.name: ease-snap
motion.purpose: A value that lands rather than settles.

motion.name: m-click
motion.purpose: A control answering a press. A thirty-second note while the clock runs.

motion.name: m-panel
motion.purpose: A pane changing; the verso turning on a stage change. A sixteenth.

motion.name: m-sweep
motion.purpose: The whole spread turning on a new lesson. An eighth.

motion.name: m-enter
motion.purpose: Ink landing on paper: the arrival of a page.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.purpose: A page turns about the binding. Eight degrees is a page being turned by someone reading it; forty is a page being thrown.

motion.name: beat-ms
motion.value: published from the transport at runtime
motion.purpose: While the clock runs, conductor.ts publishes the live tempo and its subdivisions, motion constants become musical values, and a route change lands on the next eighth. Stopped, everything falls back to the fixed values above.

components.name: Rocker
components.description: The default control: a ruled rectangle with a stamped label. The press goes into the page.
components.css: .ds-rocker{font-family:var(--font-label);font-size:max(11px,.6875rem);font-weight:500;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--ink-2);background:transparent;border:1px solid var(--rule-2);border-radius:2px;padding:.5rem 1.25rem;min-height:2.375rem;cursor:pointer;transition:color 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),background 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),box-shadow 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)}.ds-rocker:hover{color:var(--ink);background:var(--paper-2);border-color:var(--rule-3)}.ds-rocker:active{box-shadow:inset 0 2px 4px rgba(27,26,23,.18)}.ds-rocker:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--vermillion);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Rocker, engaged
components.description: The same control latched on. Vermillion label, border and wash, because it is running.

components.name: Tape
components.description: The one that commits. A strip of vermillion tape stuck to the page, torn at both ends by two fixed-width pseudo-elements so the tear stays the same size whatever the label says.

components.name: Chalk
components.description: The second commitment: the same rectangle struck in ink rather than vermillion, for an action that matters but is not the one thing the page is asking for.

components.name: Switch
components.description: The one fully rounded control in the design, because a switch is a switch: a rounded slot with a travelling knob.

components.name: Field
components.description: A ruled box on the page, set in the reading face, with its plate label engraved above it.

components.name: Stave row
components.description: A contents entry printed on its own five-line stave with a real Bravura bass clef at its head. The ruling is the paper the row sits on, knocked out behind the words; the entry you are on takes a vermillion rule in the margin, because a fill would cover the ruling that makes it a stave.
components.css: .ds-stave-list{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column}.ds-stave-row{position:relative;width:100%;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1rem 1.9rem minmax(0,1fr);align-items:center;gap:.5rem;padding:.5rem .25rem;min-height:calc(28px + 1.5rem);text-align:left;border:0;background:transparent;color:var(--ink-2);cursor:pointer;background-image:repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom,var(--stave) 0,var(--stave) 1px,transparent 1px,transparent 7px);background-repeat:no-repeat;background-position:left center;background-size:100% 29px;transition:color 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)}.ds-stave-row:hover{color:var(--ink)}.ds-clef{font-family:"Bravura",serif;font-style:normal;font-size:1.375rem;line-height:1;color:var(--ink-4);transform:translateY(-.06em)}.ds-clef::before{content:"\E062"}.ds-stave-num{font-family:var(--font-title);font-size:1.25rem;font-weight:500;font-variant-numeric:lining-nums tabular-nums;color:var(--ink-3)}.ds-stave-text{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;min-width:0}.ds-stave-name{font-family:var(--font);font-size:1rem;text-shadow:0 0 3px var(--paper),0 0 3px var(--paper),0 0 7px var(--paper)}.ds-stave-blurb{font-family:var(--font);font-size:.8125rem;color:var(--ink-3);text-shadow:0 0 3px var(--paper),0 0 3px var(--paper),0 0 7px var(--paper)}.ds-stave-row.ds-here{color:var(--ink)}.ds-stave-row.ds-here::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:-.5rem;top:12%;bottom:12%;width:2px;background:var(--vermillion)}.ds-stave-row:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--vermillion);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Section tabs
components.description: The section rail across the head of the working page. Divided by vertical rules rather than gaps, so it reads as one strip cut from the same sheet.
components.css: .ds-tabs{display:flex;align-items:stretch;height:3.5rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule);background:var(--paper)}.ds-tab{position:relative;flex:none;display:flex;align-items:center;padding:0 1.25rem;border:0;border-right:1px solid var(--rule);background:transparent;font-family:var(--font);font-size:1rem;color:var(--ink-3);white-space:nowrap;cursor:pointer;transition:color 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1),background 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)}.ds-tab:first-child{border-left:1px solid var(--rule)}.ds-tab:hover{color:var(--ink);background:var(--paper-2)}.ds-tab[aria-current="page"]{color:var(--vermillion)}.ds-tab[aria-current="page"]::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:-1px;height:2px;background:var(--vermillion)}.ds-tab:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--vermillion);outline-offset:-3px}

components.name: Fore-edge index
components.description: Tabs cut into the outer edge of the book, sitting on the stand rather than on the page. Rotated to run up the edge; hovering slides one out, which is what a hand does to a tab.

components.name: The binding
components.description: Where a workspace opens as a spread the two pages meet at a real fold: the gutter itself, one lit hairline down its centre, and a curl hung off each side that darkens whichever page is under it. Drawn in three parts, or it reads as a dark stripe.
components.html:
Say degree, note name and expected function before every click. The objective is not one memorised box.

Workspace

components.name: Transport strip
components.description: The instrument along the bottom edge: a machine bolted to the stand, not a page with controls printed on it. The play key is full-bleed into the corner so it can be hit by feel, and it is the one vermillion fill in the chrome. While the clock runs it goes to ink, so a stopped transport and a running one are never the same colour in the same place.

narrative.overview:
This is not a page you read. It is a page you play from, propped on a stand with both of your hands on an instrument, and every decision in the system follows from that. The book is open to a spread: the section's contents on the left, today's work on the right, the instrument docked in a strip along the bottom edge. Nothing floats over anything, because nothing on a stand does.

The material is warm ivory paper on a dark blue-black stand, and paper is the material rather than a theme. Two things are dark, and both are objects rather than themes: the stand the book lies on, and the instrument strip bolted to the foot of it, which is a machine and reads as one. Depth is what paper does: the book casts a real shadow onto the stand, a raised element takes a fine white top edge, and a well is cut into the sheet as darker stock. Nothing here is glass, so nothing has anything to blur.

Three things carry the look. The stave is the grid: lists are set on real five-line staves with a real SMuFL clef at the head of each line, and the ruling is the paper a row is printed on rather than a divider drawn between rows. Four hands, never mixed: Playfair strikes the title, Source Serif prints everything read, Inter is stamped small and tracked as the engraved plate label above a control, and Caveat writes in the margin in pencil blue. Vermillion is live: the red marks what is running, what is current and what to press — never what is important — so a page with nothing running and nothing to press carries no red at all, and that is the correct amount.
keyCharacteristics: Paper is the ground. Two things are dark and both are objects rather than themes: the stand the book lies on, and the instrument strip bolted to the foot of it. There is one ground; a book does not have a night mode.
A workspace opens as a spread. Reading on the verso, the instrument on the recto, and a real binding down the middle that both pages curve into.
The page is printed first, annotated in pencil second, and worked from third. Anything the interface must communicate is printed; the pencil is beside it.
Lists are set on staves. Rules are what a row sits on, not what separates it.
Everything interactive is a ruled rectangle at a 2px trim. The only fully rounded control is a switch.
Four inks with four jobs: ink reads, vermillion is live, pencil annotates, moss is a measurement taken off the player.
Depth is cast shadow, a lit top edge, and a milled well. No backdrop-filter anywhere.
Ink lands on paper, and pages turn. Arrival is a settle and a darkening; changing what is on a page turns it about the binding.
The fore-edge carries an index. Four tabs cut into the outer edge of the book, always in the same order and the same position.
Motion is governed by the transport. While the clock runs, durations are musical values and a route change lands on the next eighth.

rules.name: The Vermillion Is Live Rule
rules.body: Red marks what is running, what is current, and what to press. It never marks what is important. Audit test: if you removed every running clock and every pressable control from a screen and any vermillion remained, that vermillion is wrong.

rules.name: The Four Jobs Rule
rules.body: Every colour on the page answers one question. Ink: is this read? Vermillion: is this live? Pencil: is this an aside in the margin? Moss: was this measured off the player? A value that answers two of them has been reached for out of habit.

rules.name: The Mark Ink Rule
rules.body: --ink-4 is for marks, never for words. It measures 2.7:1 on paper. If it is setting a word, the word is not meant to be read, and the answer is --ink-3 rather than a lighter grey.

rules.name: The Redundant Code Rule
rules.body: Every colour signal is paired with a word or a glyph in the markup. On the neck a role carries hue, an ink step, a ring and a fill, never hue alone.

rules.name: The Four Hands Rule
rules.body: Playfair strikes, Source Serif prints, Inter stamps, Caveat writes in the margin. Reach for Playfair through --font-title only, and only for a struck page title, the wordmark, or a numeral. --font-display stays on the printer's serif: fourteen stylesheets ask for it by name, and pointing it at the didone puts the entire interface into italic — lesson titles and the word PASSED included.

rules.name: The Positive Tracking Rule
rules.body: Tracking is zero on anything set in a serif, because a serif on a page wants its designed fit. The didone comes in a hair at display size (-.015em) where its own fit opens up. The only place tracking goes far is the stamped label, where it goes far positive (.14em, .22em) — 11px uppercase without tracking is a smudge.

rules.name: The Small Didone Rule
rules.body: A didone has hairlines. Set it small and they disappear. Playfair below --t-h3 is a bug.

rules.name: The Real Glyph Rule
rules.body: A clef, a notehead, a time signature and a repeat sign are drawn in Bravura, never in a Unicode lookalike. Every symbol stack ends in Bravura, so a register whose first-choice face is missing loses its handwriting and keeps its engraving rather than falling through to a text font that draws a quarter note as a lowercase box.

rules.name: The Scrolling Column Rule
rules.body: A scrolling flex column never shrinks what it is scrolling: .page > * and .leaf > * are flex-shrink: 0. Without it a child whose automatic minimum is zero — anything with an overflow of its own, or an explicit min-height: 0 — collapses to its padding and lets its contents spill out and be clipped, silently.

rules.name: The Independent Pages Rule
rules.body: The stand does not scroll. The verso scrolls, the recto scrolls, and the transport is not part of the document.

rules.name: The Recto Measures Itself Rule
rules.body: Any minimum inside the right page is measured against the recto, not the viewport. A grid that adds up to less than the window can still add up to more than the page it is printed on.

rules.name: The Fold Owns The Curl Rule
rules.body: The shading either side of the binding hangs off the fold, not off the two pages. Painted on the panes it stops wherever the shorter pane stops — the workspace is sticky and capped at the viewport — and a binding shaded for two thirds of its length is a stripe again.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: --blur is none and --depth-panel is none. Do not apply backdrop-filter to anything. A panel is a ruled box, not a pane.

rules.name: The Press Goes In Rule
rules.body: Active states push into the surface with an inset shadow. Nothing lifts on press; only the strip of tape, which is stuck to the page rather than printed on it, rises a pixel on hover.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: A panel carries no fill and no shadow — the page is already the right colour, and a second ivory inside the first only muddies the rule that separates them.

rules.name: The Ruled Rectangle Rule
rules.body: Interactive means a hard-cornered rectangle at 2px. The switch is the one exception, and it earns it by being a switch.

rules.name: The Trimmed Corner Rule
rules.body: 10px belongs to the three physical objects — verso, recto, transport — and to nothing inside them.

rules.name: The No Radius In Focus Rule
rules.body: Never set border-radius inside a focus rule. It reshapes the element rather than the outline.

rules.name: The Plate Label Rule
rules.body: A control's label is engraved above it and does not change. What the control currently says goes inside the control.

rules.name: The Margin Is Never Load-Bearing Rule
rules.body: Anything the interface must communicate is printed. The pencil hand is written next to it, and a screen that still works with every .annot deleted is correct.

rules.name: The Nut Is The Line Rule
rules.body: The first fret in a row drops its left border, because the string-name column already draws the nut as a heavy rule and a hairline a pixel to its right reads as the nut printed twice.

dos: Do let paper be the ground and keep the stand as the only dark surface.
Do spend vermillion only on what is running, current, or pressable. If nothing on the screen is any of those, the screen carries no red.
Do set every list on staves, with a real Bravura clef at the head of each line and the ruling knocked out behind the words.
Do give every interactive element a 2px hard corner, and reserve 10px for the verso, the recto and the transport strip.
Do engrave a plate label above a control in Inter at 11px uppercase, tracked .14em.
Do keep --ink-3 as the floor for anything read, and --ink-4 for marks only.
Do self-host every face and every symbol font under /fonts.
Do put flex-shrink: 0 on the children of any scrolling flex column.
Do theme the browser's own furniture — selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring, and tabular figures — from this palette.
Do open a split workspace as a spread, with the binding between the pages and no gap standing them off it.
Do turn a page about the binding when what is printed on it changes.
Do keep the fore-edge index in one order and one position.
Do collapse every entrance to its final state under prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't point --font-display at Playfair. The didone is reached through --font-title only.
Don't set Playfair below --t-h3; its hairlines disappear.
Don't apply backdrop-filter to anything. There is no glass here.
Don't set border-radius inside a focus rule.
Don't track a serif. Tracking is zero on anything set in Source Serif or Playfair body copy, and far positive only on the stamped label.
Don't use --ink-4 for words. It measures 2.7:1.
Don't rank a note's role by hue alone — the ink step, the ring and the fill have to carry it too.
Don't introduce a second ground or a theme attribute. There is one ground; a rule gated on a theme that is never set is a rule that does nothing while the value it was written to correct stays live.
Don't put a fill behind a row that is set on a stave. It covers the ruling that makes it a stave; mark it in the margin instead.
Don't let a control inside a page borrow the page's 10px corner.
Don't hotlink a font, image, script or stylesheet from a third-party host. They are blocked outright here and the failure is silent.
Don't measure a minimum inside the right page against the viewport.
Don't put a rule between two pages of a spread. The fold is the divider, and a line beside it reads as a scratch down the binding.
Don't draw the fold on a stacked layout. One column has no gutter.
Don't turn the stand, the fore-edge index or the instrument strip. Only pages turn.
Don't remount a live tool to animate it. Hold the turn as state.
Don't reach for --bg when you mean the page. The legacy token file repoints it at the shaded stock; the page is --paper.
